newsitem.title: INDIA: India HPCL 96/97 1st half sales 7.39 MT.
newsitem.headline: India HPCL 96/97 1st half sales 7.39 MT.

text.p: India's state-run Hindustan Petroleum Corp Ltd (HPCL) said its sales for the six months ended September 30, 1996 rose to 7.39 million tonnes, up from 6.82 million tonnes during the same period a year ago.
The sales growth, at 8.4 percent, was higher than the 6.5 percent industry average, it said in a statement on Friday.
The turnover for the period was 81.43 billion rupees, a rise of about 17 percent over the year ago figures, HPCL said.
"The refining performance of HPCL during the first half of the year has been at a peak level with total crude throughput of 5.90 million tonnes," it said.
HPCL said its sales and profit after tax in the first half of 1996/97 (April-March) were the highest ever.

Net profit increased to 3.01 billion rupees against 2.54 billion in the year ago period. The earnings per share and cash earnings per share are 28.91 rupees and 44.32 rupees respectively, HPCL said after a board meeting on Thursday.
It said it had commissioned LPG import facilities worth 1.75 billion rupees at Mangalore. Other major expansion projects are going according to schedule, it said.
"In collaboration with Saudi Aramco, the corporation is in advanced stage of finalising the location for its third joint venture grassroot refinery in the state of Punjab," it said.
